i18n.he: וַיְהִ֗י כִּשְׁמֹ֙עַ֙ הַמֶּ֣לֶךְ חִזְקִיָּ֔הוּ וַיִּקְרַ֖ע אֶת־בְּגָדָ֑יו וַיִּתְכַּ֣ס בַּשָּׂ֔ק וַיָּבֹ֖א בֵּ֥ית יְהוָֽה׃

i18n.en: And he sent Eliakim, who was over the house, and Shebna the scribe, and the elders of the priests, covered with sackcloth, to Isaiah the son of Amoz, the prophet.
i18n.he: וַ֠יִּשְׁלַח אֶת־אֶלְיָקִ֨ים אֲשֶׁר־עַל־הַבַּ֜יִת וְאֵ֣ת ׀ שֶׁבְנָ֣א הַסּוֹפֵ֗ר וְאֵת֙ זִקְנֵ֣י הַכֹּהֲנִ֔ים מִתְכַּסִּ֖ים בַּשַּׂקִּ֑ים אֶל־יְשַֽׁעְיָ֥הוּ בֶן־אָמ֖וֹץ הַנָּבִֽיא׃

notes.official:
*ʾĂšer ʿal-habbayiṯ* “who was over the house”: the title of the palace official, the phrase that the stable 22:15 renders “who is over the house” (overlay `lexical-cruxes-isaiah-22`). ASV and JPS 1917 have “who was over the household,” NJPS “who was in charge of the palace” (checked). The line keeps one English phrase for the one office in Isaiah, as at 36:3, 22 (overlay `lexical-cruxes-isaiah-22`, extended to this verse). *Hassôp̄ēr* is “the scribe” in ASV, JPS 1917 and NJPS (“Shebna, the scribe”; checked).

2 Kgs 19:2 differs only in word order (“Isaiah the prophet, the son of Amoz”) and writes *wᵉšeḇnāʾ* without the object marker (MT, checked); the sense is the same.

paragraphs.text: וַיֹּאמְר֣וּ אֵלָ֗יו כֹּ֚ה אָמַ֣ר חִזְקִיָּ֔הוּ יוֹם־צָרָ֧ה וְתוֹכֵחָ֛ה וּנְאָצָ֖ה הַיּ֣וֹם הַזֶּ֑ה כִּ֣י בָ֤אוּ בָנִים֙ עַד־מַשְׁבֵּ֔ר וְכֹ֥חַ אַ֖יִן לְלֵדָֽה׃

i18n.en: And they said to him, “Thus says Hezekiah: This day is a day of trouble, and of rebuke, and of contempt; for the children have come to the birth, and there is no strength to bring forth.
i18n.he: וַיֹּאמְר֣וּ אֵלָ֗יו כֹּ֚ה אָמַ֣ר חִזְקִיָּ֔הוּ יוֹם־צָרָ֧ה וְתוֹכֵחָ֛ה וּנְאָצָ֖ה הַיּ֣וֹם הַזֶּ֑ה כִּ֣י בָ֤אוּ בָנִים֙ עַד־מַשְׁבֵּ֔ר וְכֹ֥חַ אַ֖יִן לְלֵדָֽה׃

notes.official: *Nᵉʾāṣāh* “contempt”: ASV and JPS 1917 have “contumely,” NJPS “disgrace” (checked); “contempt” is the current word for ASV's sense. *Kî ḇāʾû ḇānîm ʿaḏ-mašbēr* “for the children have come to the birth”: *mašbēr* is the opening of the womb. NJPS has “The babes have reached the birthstool,” with the note “I.e., the situation is desperate, and we are at a loss” (checked). The line keeps ASV's image (overlay `lexical-cruxes-isaiah-37`). 2 Kgs 19:3 is identical in MT (checked).

paragraphs.translit: wayyōʾmərū ʾēlāyw kōh ʾāmar ḥizqiyyāhū yōm-ṣārāh wətōkēḥāh ūnəʾāṣāh hayyōm hazzeh kī bāʾū bānīm ʿad-mašbēr wəkōaḥ ʾayin ləlēdāh

paragraphs.text: אוּלַ֡י יִשְׁמַע֩ יְהוָ֨ה אֱלֹהֶ֜יךָ אֵ֣ת ׀ דִּבְרֵ֣י רַב־שָׁקֵ֗ה אֲשֶׁר֩ שְׁלָח֨וֹ מֶֽלֶךְ־אַשּׁ֤וּר ׀ אֲדֹנָיו֙ לְחָרֵף֙ אֱלֹהִ֣ים חַ֔י וְהוֹכִ֙יחַ֙ בַּדְּבָרִ֔ים אֲשֶׁ֥ר שָׁמַ֖ע יְהוָ֣ה אֱלֹהֶ֑יךָ וְנָשָׂ֣אתָ תְפִלָּ֔ה בְּעַ֥ד הַשְּׁאֵרִ֖ית הַנִּמְצָאָֽה׃

i18n.en: Perhaps YHWH your God will hear the words of the Rabshakeh, whom the king of Assyria his master has sent to defy the living God, and will rebuke the words that YHWH your God has heard; so lift up a prayer for the remnant that is left.”
i18n.he: אוּלַ֡י יִשְׁמַע֩ יְהוָ֨ה אֱלֹהֶ֜יךָ אֵ֣ת ׀ דִּבְרֵ֣י רַב־שָׁקֵ֗ה אֲשֶׁר֩ שְׁלָח֨וֹ מֶֽלֶךְ־אַשּׁ֤וּר ׀ אֲדֹנָיו֙ לְחָרֵף֙ אֱלֹהִ֣ים חַ֔י וְהוֹכִ֙יחַ֙ בַּדְּבָרִ֔ים אֲשֶׁ֥ר שָׁמַ֖ע יְהוָ֣ה אֱלֹהֶ֑יךָ וְנָשָׂ֣אתָ תְפִלָּ֔ה בְּעַ֥ד הַשְּׁאֵרִ֖ית הַנִּמְצָאָֽה׃

notes.official:
*Lᵉḥārēp̄ ʾĕlōhîm ḥay* “to defy the living God”: the noun has no article, and the adjective is singular (*ḥay*), as again at 37:17. Elsewhere the phrase has the plural adjective, *ʾĕlōhîm ḥayyîm* (Deut 5:23 [Eng. 5:26]; 1 Sam 17:26; Jer 10:10; MT checked). The singular adjective marks the referent as YHWH. ASV, JPS 1917 and NJPS all print “the living God” (checked), and the line follows them with capital “God” (overlay `elohim-el-eloah-monotheistic-formula-isaiah`). The words are Hezekiah's own message to Isaiah, describing the purpose of the Rabshakeh's mission. *Ḥrp* is “defy” here and at 37:17, 23, 24 (ASV); JPS 1917 has “taunt,” NJPS “blaspheme.” The line keeps “blaspheme” for *gdp* (37:6, 23).

*Raḇ-šāqēh* is “the Rabshakeh,” a title with the article (wave ruling 7; overlay `rabshakeh-title-isaiah`), as NJPS prints it (checked); ASV and JPS 1917 treat it as a name. *Haššᵉʾērîṯ hannimṣāʾāh* “the remnant that is left” (ASV) is the remnant noun *šᵉʾērîṯ* (central `she-erit-remnant-cross-corpus-theological-keyword`); NJPS has “the surviving remnant.” 2 Kgs 19:4 reads *kol-diḇrê* “all the words of” (MT, checked).

paragraphs.text: וַיָּבֹ֗אוּ עַבְדֵ֛י הַמֶּ֥לֶךְ חִזְקִיָּ֖הוּ אֶל־יְשַׁעְיָֽהוּ׃

i18n.en: So the servants of King Hezekiah came to Isaiah.
i18n.he: וַיָּבֹ֗אוּ עַבְדֵ֛י הַמֶּ֥לֶךְ חִזְקִיָּ֖הוּ אֶל־יְשַׁעְיָֽהוּ׃

paragraphs.text: וַיֹּ֤אמֶר אֲלֵיהֶם֙ יְשַֽׁעְיָ֔הוּ כֹּ֥ה תֹאמְר֖וּן אֶל־אֲדֹנֵיכֶ֑ם כֹּ֣ה ׀ אָמַ֣ר יְהוָ֗ה אַל־תִּירָא֙ מִפְּנֵ֤י הַדְּבָרִים֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר שָׁמַ֔עְתָּ אֲשֶׁ֧ר גִּדְּפ֛וּ נַעֲרֵ֥י מֶלֶךְ־אַשּׁ֖וּר אוֹתִֽי׃

i18n.en: And Isaiah said to them, “Thus you shall say to your master: Thus says YHWH: Do not be afraid of the words that you have heard, with which the servants of the king of Assyria have blasphemed me.
i18n.he: וַיֹּ֤אמֶר אֲלֵיהֶם֙ יְשַֽׁעְיָ֔הוּ כֹּ֥ה תֹאמְר֖וּן אֶל־אֲדֹנֵיכֶ֑ם כֹּ֣ה ׀ אָמַ֣ר יְהוָ֗ה אַל־תִּירָא֙ מִפְּנֵ֤י הַדְּבָרִים֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר שָׁמַ֔עְתָּ אֲשֶׁ֧ר גִּדְּפ֛וּ נַעֲרֵ֥י מֶלֶךְ־אַשּׁ֖וּר אוֹתִֽי׃

notes.official: *Naʿărê meleḵ-ʾaššûr* “the servants of the king of Assyria”: *naʿar* is a young man or attendant, a different noun from *ʿeḇeḏ* “servant” (37:5, 24). ASV and JPS 1917 print “servants” for both. NJPS marks the difference with “the minions of the king of Assyria,” and has “ministers” for *ʿaḇdê* at 37:5 (checked). The line keeps the public-domain wording and leaves the distinction to this note (overlay `lexical-cruxes-isaiah-37`). *Giddᵉp̄û* is “blasphemed,” as at 37:23. 2 Kgs 19:6 has *lāhem* for *ʾălêhem* (MT, checked), with no difference of sense.

paragraphs.translit: wayyōʾmer ʾălēhem yəšaʿyāhū kōh tōʾmərūn ʾel-ʾădōnēkem kōh | ʾāmar YHWH ʾal-tīrāʾ mippənē haddəbārīm ʾăšer šāmaʿtā ʾăšer giddəpū naʿărē melek-ʾaššūr ʾōtī

paragraphs.text: הִנְנִ֨י נוֹתֵ֥ן בּוֹ֙ ר֔וּחַ וְשָׁמַ֥ע שְׁמוּעָ֖ה וְשָׁ֣ב אֶל־אַרְצ֑וֹ וְהִפַּלְתִּ֥יו בַּחֶ֖רֶב בְּאַרְצֽוֹ׃

i18n.en: Behold, I will put a spirit in him, and he shall hear tidings and return to his own land; and I will make him fall by the sword in his own land.”
i18n.he: הִנְנִ֨י נוֹתֵ֥ן בּוֹ֙ ר֔וּחַ וְשָׁמַ֥ע שְׁמוּעָ֖ה וְשָׁ֣ב אֶל־אַרְצ֑וֹ וְהִפַּלְתִּ֥יו בַּחֶ֖רֶב בְּאַרְצֽוֹ׃

notes.official: *Hinnî nôṯēn bô rûaḥ* “I will put a spirit in him”: lower-case “spirit” (overlay `ruach-divine-spirit-lower-case-isaiah`). ASV and JPS 1917 keep the literal phrase. NJPS interprets it, “I will delude him,” with the note “Lit. ‘put a spirit in’” (checked). The verse does not say what kind of *rûaḥ* it is, an impulse, a fear or a deceiving spirit like the *rûaḥ šeqer* of 1 Kgs 22:22 (MT checked), and the line does not decide. *Šᵉmûʿāh* is “tidings” (ASV; JPS 1917 “rumour”). The prophecy is carried out in 37:9 and 37:37–38. 2 Kgs 19:7 has *lᵉʾarṣô* for Isaiah's *ʾel-ʾarṣô* “to his own land” (MT, checked), with no difference of sense.

paragraphs.translit: hinnī nōtēn bō rūaḥ wəšāmaʿ šəmūʿāh wəšāb ʾel-ʾarṣō wəhippaltīw baḥereb bəʾarṣō

paragraphs.text: וַיָּ֙שָׁב֙ רַב־שָׁקֵ֔ה וַיִּמְצָא֙ אֶת־מֶ֣לֶךְ אַשּׁ֔וּר נִלְחָ֖ם עַל־לִבְנָ֑ה כִּ֣י שָׁמַ֔ע כִּ֥י נָסַ֖ע מִלָּכִֽישׁ׃

i18n.en: So the Rabshakeh returned, and found the king of Assyria fighting against Libnah; for he had heard that he had departed from Lachish.
i18n.he: וַיָּ֙שָׁב֙ רַב־שָׁקֵ֔ה וַיִּמְצָא֙ אֶת־מֶ֣לֶךְ אַשּׁ֔וּר נִלְחָ֖ם עַל־לִבְנָ֑ה כִּ֣י שָׁמַ֔ע כִּ֥י נָסַ֖ע מִלָּכִֽישׁ׃

notes.official: “The Rabshakeh,” with the article (overlay `rabshakeh-title-isaiah`; NJPS “The Rabshakeh, meanwhile,” checked). 2 Kgs 19:8 is identical in MT (checked).

paragraphs.translit: wayyāšāb rab-šāqēh wayyimṣāʾ ʾet-melek ʾaššūr nilḥām ʿal-libnāh kī šāmaʿ kī nāsaʿ millākīš

paragraphs.text: וַיִּשְׁמַ֗ע עַל־תִּרְהָ֤קָה מֶֽלֶךְ־כּוּשׁ֙ לֵאמֹ֔ר יָצָ֖א לְהִלָּחֵ֣ם אִתָּ֑ךְ וַיִּשְׁמַע֙ וַיִּשְׁלַ֣ח מַלְאָכִ֔ים אֶל־חִזְקִיָּ֖הוּ לֵאמֹֽר׃

i18n.en: And he heard it said concerning Tirhakah king of Cush, “He has come out to fight against you.” And when he heard it, he sent messengers to Hezekiah, saying,
i18n.he: וַיִּשְׁמַ֗ע עַל־תִּרְהָ֤קָה מֶֽלֶךְ־כּוּשׁ֙ לֵאמֹ֔ר יָצָ֖א לְהִלָּחֵ֣ם אִתָּ֑ךְ וַיִּשְׁמַע֙ וַיִּשְׁלַ֣ח מַלְאָכִ֔ים אֶל־חִזְקִיָּ֖הוּ לֵאמֹֽר׃

notes.official:
*Tirhāqāh meleḵ-kûš* “Tirhakah king of Cush” (overlay `cush-names-isaiah`): ASV and JPS 1917 have “Ethiopia,” NJPS “Nubia” (checked). The king is the Kushite ruler of Egypt known in Egyptian sources as Taharqa (recalled, not verified).

2 Kgs 19:9 differs in three places (MT, checked). It reads *ʾel-tirhāqāh* for *ʿal-tirhāqāh*. It adds *hinnēh*, “Behold, he has come out.” And where Isaiah repeats *wayyišmaʿ* “and when he heard it,” Kings has *wayyāšoḇ*, “and he again (sent).” The line translates Isaiah's text with ASV and JPS 1917 (“And when he heard it”).

paragraphs.translit: wayyišmaʿ ʿal-tirhāqāh melek-kūš lēʾmōr yāṣāʾ ləhillāḥēm ʾittāk wayyišmaʿ wayyišlaḥ malʾākīm ʾel-ḥizqiyyāhū lēʾmōr

paragraphs.text: כֹּ֣ה תֹאמְר֗וּן אֶל־חִזְקִיָּ֤הוּ מֶֽלֶךְ־יְהוּדָה֙ לֵאמֹ֔ר אַל־יַשִּֽׁאֲךָ֣ אֱלֹהֶ֔יךָ אֲשֶׁ֥ר אַתָּ֛ה בּוֹטֵ֥חַ בּ֖וֹ לֵאמֹ֑ר לֹ֤א תִנָּתֵן֙ יְר֣וּשָׁלִַ֔ם בְּיַ֖ד מֶ֥לֶךְ אַשּֽׁוּר׃

i18n.en: “Thus you shall speak to Hezekiah king of Judah, saying: Do not let your God in whom you trust deceive you, saying, Jerusalem shall not be given into the hand of the king of Assyria.
i18n.he: כֹּ֣ה תֹאמְר֗וּן אֶל־חִזְקִיָּ֤הוּ מֶֽלֶךְ־יְהוּדָה֙ לֵאמֹ֔ר אַל־יַשִּֽׁאֲךָ֣ אֱלֹהֶ֔יךָ אֲשֶׁ֥ר אַתָּ֛ה בּוֹטֵ֥חַ בּ֖וֹ לֵאמֹ֑ר לֹ֤א תִנָּתֵן֙ יְר֣וּשָׁלִַ֔ם בְּיַ֖ד מֶ֥לֶךְ אַשּֽׁוּר׃

notes.official: *ʾAl-yaššîʾăḵā* “Do not let … deceive you” is the verb of 36:14 (“Do not let Hezekiah deceive you”), now with Hezekiah's God as subject. ASV has “deceive,” JPS 1917 “beguile,” NJPS “mislead” (checked). 2 Kgs 19:10 is identical in sense (MT, checked).

paragraphs.translit: kōh tōʾmərūn ʾel-ḥizqiyyāhū melek-yəhūdāh lēʾmōr ʾal-yaššiʾăkā ʾĕlōhēkā ʾăšer ʾattāh bōṭēaḥ bō lēʾmōr lōʾ tinnātēn yərūšālim bəyad melek ʾaššūr

paragraphs.text: הִנֵּ֣ה ׀ אַתָּ֣ה שָׁמַ֗עְתָּ אֲשֶׁ֨ר עָשׂ֜וּ מַלְכֵ֥י אַשּׁ֛וּר לְכָל־הָאֲרָצ֖וֹת לְהַחֲרִימָ֑ם וְאַתָּ֖ה תִּנָּצֵֽל׃

i18n.en: Behold, you have heard what the kings of Assyria have done to all the lands, devoting them to destruction; and shall you be delivered?
i18n.he: הִנֵּ֣ה ׀ אַתָּ֣ה שָׁמַ֗עְתָּ אֲשֶׁ֨ר עָשׂ֜וּ מַלְכֵ֥י אַשּׁ֛וּר לְכָל־הָאֲרָצ֖וֹת לְהַחֲרִימָ֑ם וְאַתָּ֖ה תִּנָּצֵֽל׃

notes.official: *Lᵉhaḥărîmām* “devoting them to destruction” (central `cherem-devote-to-destruction-cross-corpus`, as 34:2): ASV and JPS 1917 have “by destroying them utterly,” NJPS “how they have annihilated them” (checked). The line keeps the root “devote” visible. The Assyrian speaker uses the Hebrew word for the war ban of Josh 6:21; 10:28–40. 2 Kgs 19:11 adds the object marker *ʾēṯ* (MT, checked).

paragraphs.translit: hinnēh | ʾattāh šāmaʿtā ʾăšer ʿāśū malkē ʾaššūr ləkol-hāʾărāṣōt ləhaḥărīmām wəʾattāh tinnāṣēl

paragraphs.text: הַהִצִּ֨ילוּ אוֹתָ֜ם אֱלֹהֵ֤י הַגּוֹיִם֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר הִשְׁחִ֣יתוּ אֲבוֹתַ֔י אֶת־גּוֹזָ֖ן וְאֶת־חָרָ֑ן וְרֶ֥צֶף וּבְנֵי־עֶ֖דֶן אֲשֶׁ֥ר בִּתְלַשָּֽׂר׃

i18n.en: Have the gods of the nations delivered them, which my fathers destroyed, Gozan and Haran and Rezeph, and the children of Eden who were in Telassar?
i18n.he: הַהִצִּ֨ילוּ אוֹתָ֜ם אֱלֹהֵ֤י הַגּוֹיִם֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר הִשְׁחִ֣יתוּ אֲבוֹתַ֔י אֶת־גּוֹזָ֖ן וְאֶת־חָרָ֑ן וְרֶ֥צֶף וּבְנֵי־עֶ֖דֶן אֲשֶׁ֥ר בִּתְלַשָּֽׂר׃

notes.official:
*Bᵉnê-ʿeḏen ʾăšer bitlaśśār* “the children of Eden who were in Telassar”: this Eden is an Aramean state on the middle Euphrates, called Bit-Adini in Assyrian sources (recalled, not verified). It is the *bêṯ ʿeḏen* of Amos 1:5 and the *ʿeḏen* of Ezek 27:23 (MT checked), not the garden. The consonants are the same, but MT vocalizes the state *ʿeḏen* and the garden *ʿēḏen* (Gen 2:8, MT checked). ASV and JPS 1917 have “the children of Eden,” NJPS “the Bethedenites in Telassar” (checked). The line keeps the public-domain wording (overlay `lexical-cruxes-isaiah-37`); nothing in the verse refers to the garden.

*ʾĂḇôṯay* “my fathers” (ASV, JPS 1917); NJPS has “my predecessors,” with the note “Lit. ‘fathers’” (checked). The gods of the nations are lower case (overlay `elohim-el-eloah-monotheistic-formula-isaiah`). 2 Kgs 19:12 has the Piel *šiḥăṯû* for Isaiah's Hiphil *hišḥîṯû* and spells *bitlaʾśśār* (MT, checked).

paragraphs.translit: hahiṣṣīlū ʾōtām ʾĕlōhē haggōyim ʾăšer hišḥītū ʾăbōtay ʾet-gōzān wəʾet-ḥārān wəreṣep ūbənē-ʿeden ʾăšer bitlaśśār

paragraphs.text: אַיֵּ֤ה מֶֽלֶךְ־חֲמָת֙ וּמֶ֣לֶךְ אַרְפָּ֔ד וּמֶ֖לֶךְ לָעִ֣יר סְפַרְוָ֑יִם הֵנַ֖ע וְעִוָּֽה׃

i18n.en: Where is the king of Hamath, and the king of Arpad, and the king of the city of Sepharvaim, of Hena, and of Ivvah?”
i18n.he: אַיֵּ֤ה מֶֽלֶךְ־חֲמָת֙ וּמֶ֣לֶךְ אַרְפָּ֔ד וּמֶ֖לֶךְ לָעִ֣יר סְפַרְוָ֑יִם הֵנַ֖ע וְעִוָּֽה׃

notes.official: *Meleḵ lāʿîr sᵉp̄arwāyim hēnaʿ wᵉʿiwwāh* “the king of the city of Sepharvaim, of Hena, and of Ivvah”: ASV and JPS 1917 take *lāʿîr* as “of the city.” NJPS reads it as a further place name, “the kings of Lair, Sepharvaim, Hena, and Ivvah” (checked). The line keeps ASV (overlay `lexical-cruxes-isaiah-37`). Hamath, Arpad and Sepharvaim were already named in the Rabshakeh's speech (36:19). 2 Kgs 19:13 has *ʾayyô* for *ʾayyēh* “Where is” (MT, checked).

paragraphs.translit: ʾayyēh melek-ḥămāt ūmelek ʾarpād ūmelek lāʿīr səparwāyim hēnaʿ wəʿiwwāh

paragraphs.text: וַיִּקַּ֨ח חִזְקִיָּ֧הוּ אֶת־הַסְּפָרִ֛ים מִיַּ֥ד הַמַּלְאָכִ֖ים וַיִּקְרָאֵ֑הוּ וַיַּ֙עַל֙ בֵּ֣ית יְהוָ֔ה וַיִּפְרְשֵׂ֥הוּ חִזְקִיָּ֖הוּ לִפְנֵ֥י יְהוָֽה׃

i18n.en: And Hezekiah took the letter from the hand of the messengers and read it; and Hezekiah went up to the house of YHWH and spread it out before YHWH.
i18n.he: וַיִּקַּ֨ח חִזְקִיָּ֧הוּ אֶת־הַסְּפָרִ֛ים מִיַּ֥ד הַמַּלְאָכִ֖ים וַיִּקְרָאֵ֑הוּ וַיַּ֙עַל֙ בֵּ֣ית יְהוָ֔ה וַיִּפְרְשֵׂ֥הוּ חִזְקִיָּ֖הוּ לִפְנֵ֥י יְהוָֽה׃

notes.official: *Hassᵉp̄ārîm* “the letter”: the noun is plural, but both suffixes in Isaiah are singular (*wayyiqrāʾēhû* “and read it,” *wayyip̄rᵉśēhû* “and spread it out”). 2 Kgs 19:14 has the plural *wayyiqrāʾēm* “and read them” beside the singular *wayyip̄rᵉśēhû* (MT, checked). ASV, JPS 1917 and NJPS all print “the letter” (checked), and the line follows them (overlay `lexical-cruxes-isaiah-37`). At 39:1, where no singular suffix follows, *sᵉp̄ārîm* is “letters.” The document is not the sealed scroll of 29:11 (overlay `sefer-sealed-scroll-isaiah-29` governs only its listed sites).

paragraphs.translit: wayyiqqaḥ ḥizqiyyāhū ʾet-hassəpārīm miyyad hammalʾākīm wayyiqrāʾēhū wayyaʿal bēt YHWH wayyiprəśēhū ḥizqiyyāhū lipnē YHWH

paragraphs.text: וַיִּתְפַּלֵּל֙ חִזְקִיָּ֔הוּ אֶל־יְהוָ֖ה לֵאמֹֽר׃

i18n.en: And Hezekiah prayed to YHWH, saying,
i18n.he: וַיִּתְפַּלֵּל֙ חִזְקִיָּ֔הוּ אֶל־יְהוָ֖ה לֵאמֹֽר׃

notes.official: 2 Kgs 19:15 reads *wayyiṯpallēl ḥizqiyyāhû lip̄nê YHWH wayyōʾmar* “Hezekiah prayed before YHWH and said,” where Isaiah has *ʾel-YHWH lēʾmōr* “to YHWH, saying” (MT, checked).

paragraphs.translit: wayyitpallēl ḥizqiyyāhū ʾel-YHWH lēʾmōr

paragraphs.text: יְהוָ֨ה צְבָא֜וֹת אֱלֹהֵ֤י יִשְׂרָאֵל֙ יֹשֵׁ֣ב הַכְּרֻבִ֔ים אַתָּה־ה֤וּא הָֽאֱלֹהִים֙ לְבַדְּךָ֔ לְכֹ֖ל מַמְלְכ֣וֹת הָאָ֑רֶץ אַתָּ֣ה עָשִׂ֔יתָ אֶת־הַשָּׁמַ֖יִם וְאֶת־הָאָֽרֶץ׃

i18n.en: “O YHWH of hosts, the God of Israel, who is enthroned on the cherubim, you are God, you alone, of all the kingdoms of the earth; you have made the skies and the earth.
i18n.he: יְהוָ֨ה צְבָא֜וֹת אֱלֹהֵ֤י יִשְׂרָאֵל֙ יֹשֵׁ֣ב הַכְּרֻבִ֔ים אַתָּה־ה֤וּא הָֽאֱלֹהִים֙ לְבַדְּךָ֔ לְכֹ֖ל מַמְלְכ֣וֹת הָאָ֑רֶץ אַתָּ֣ה עָשִׂ֔יתָ אֶת־הַשָּׁמַ֖יִם וְאֶת־הָאָֽרֶץ׃

notes.official:
*Yōšēḇ hakkᵉrūḇîm* “who is enthroned on the cherubim”: the participle has no preposition, so every English version supplies one. ASV prints “that sittest [above] the cherubim,” marking the word as supplied; JPS 1917 has “that sittest upon the cherubim,” NJPS “enthroned on the Cherubim” (checked). The same fixed title stands at 1 Sam 4:4; 2 Sam 6:2; Ps 80:2; 99:1 and in the parallel 2 Kgs 19:15 (MT checked), and the corpus already prints “who is enthroned on the cherubim” at the stable 2 Sam 6:2 (2-samuel-woh). The line uses that wording, so that one title has one English form across the corpus (central `cherubim-ezek`; overlay `lexical-cruxes-isaiah-37`). The title presents the cherubim of the ark as YHWH's throne. Exod 25:22 places the divine voice “from above the cover, from between the two cherubim” (*mēʿal hakkappōreṯ mibbên šᵉnê hakkᵉrūḇîm*, MT checked), which is the basis of ASV's supplied “above.”

*ʾAttāh-hûʾ hāʾĕlōhîm lᵉḇaddᵉḵā* “you are God, you alone”: the noun has the article, which ASV and JPS 1917 render “the God.” The line has “God,” as at 45:18 *hûʾ hāʾĕlōhîm* “he is God” (overlay `elohim-el-eloah-monotheistic-formula-isaiah`); NJPS has “You alone are God of all the kingdoms of the earth” (checked). *Haššāmayim* is “the skies” in the creation merism, as at 42:5 and 45:18 (central `shamayim`).

2 Kgs 19:15 has no *ṣᵉḇāʾôṯ*: “YHWH, God of Israel” (MT, checked). The NJPS text of Isa 37:16 as retrieved reads “O LORD of Hosts, enthroned on the Cherubim!” and has no words for *ʾĕlōhê yiśrāʾēl*.

paragraphs.translit: YHWH ṣəbāʾōt ʾĕlōhē yiśrāʾēl yōšēb hakkərubīm ʾattāh-hūʾ hāʾĕlōhīm ləbaddəkā ləkōl mamləkōt hāʾāreṣ ʾattāh ʿāśītā ʾet-haššāmayim wəʾet-hāʾāreṣ

paragraphs.text: הַטֵּ֨ה יְהוָ֤ה ׀ אָזְנְךָ֙ וּֽשְׁמָ֔ע פְּקַ֧ח יְהוָ֛ה עֵינֶ֖ךָ וּרְאֵ֑ה וּשְׁמַ֗ע אֵ֚ת כָּל־דִּבְרֵ֣י סַנְחֵרִ֔יב אֲשֶׁ֣ר שָׁלַ֔ח לְחָרֵ֖ף אֱלֹהִ֥ים חָֽי׃

i18n.en: Incline your ear, O YHWH, and hear; open your eyes, O YHWH, and see; and hear all the words of Sennacherib, who has sent to defy the living God.
i18n.he: הַטֵּ֨ה יְהוָ֤ה ׀ אָזְנְךָ֙ וּֽשְׁמָ֔ע פְּקַ֧ח יְהוָ֛ה עֵינֶ֖ךָ וּרְאֵ֑ה וּשְׁמַ֗ע אֵ֚ת כָּל־דִּבְרֵ֣י סַנְחֵרִ֔יב אֲשֶׁ֣ר שָׁלַ֔ח לְחָרֵ֖ף אֱלֹהִ֥ים חָֽי׃

notes.official:
*Pᵉqaḥ YHWH ʿênᵉḵā* “open your eyes, O YHWH”: Isaiah writes the noun without the yod of the plural (עֵינֶךָ), where 2 Kgs 19:16 has עֵינֶיךָ “your eyes” (MT, checked). The Isaiah form can be read as a singular, as NJPS reads it (“open Your eye and see”), matching the singular “your ear” of the first clause. ASV and JPS 1917 read it as a defective spelling of the plural (“open thine eyes”; checked), which the segol vowel under the *nun* supports. The line keeps the plural (overlays `lexical-cruxes-isaiah-37`, `mt-qere-textual-policy-isaiah`). In 37:23 the same chapter writes the plural with yod.

*Kol-diḇrê sanḥērîḇ ʾăšer šālaḥ* “all the words of Sennacherib, who has sent”: Isaiah has *šālaḥ* without an object, which can also be read “which he has sent” (NJPS “all the words that Sennacherib has sent”), while 2 Kgs 19:16 has *ʾăšer šᵉlāḥô* “who sent him,” the Rabshakeh, and lacks *kol* (MT, checked). The line keeps ASV.

paragraphs.translit: haṭṭēh YHWH | ʾoznəkā ūšəmāʿ pəqaḥ YHWH ʿēnekā ūrəʾēh ūšəmaʿ ʾēt kol-dibrē sanḥērīb ʾăšer šālaḥ ləḥārēp ʾĕlōhīm ḥāy

paragraphs.text: אָמְנָ֖ם יְהוָ֑ה הֶחֱרִ֜יבוּ מַלְכֵ֥י אַשּׁ֛וּר אֶת־כָּל־הָאֲרָצ֖וֹת וְאֶת־אַרְצָֽם׃

i18n.en: Truly, YHWH, the kings of Assyria have laid waste all the lands and their land,
i18n.he: אָמְנָ֖ם יְהוָ֑ה הֶחֱרִ֜יבוּ מַלְכֵ֥י אַשּׁ֛וּר אֶת־כָּל־הָאֲרָצ֖וֹת וְאֶת־אַרְצָֽם׃

notes.official: *Heḥĕrîḇû … ʾeṯ-kol-hāʾărāṣôṯ wᵉʾeṯ-ʾarṣām* “have laid waste all the lands and their land”: the repetition is awkward, and 2 Kgs 19:17 reads *ʾeṯ-haggôyim wᵉʾeṯ-ʾarṣām* “the nations and their land” (MT, checked). NJPS translates the Kings reading, “all the nations and their lands,” with the note “So 2 Kings 19.17, and 13 mss. here; most mss. and editions read ‘lands’” (checked). ASV (“all the countries, and their land”) and JPS 1917 keep the Isaiah text, and so does the line (overlays `lexical-cruxes-isaiah-37`, `mt-qere-textual-policy-isaiah`).

paragraphs.translit: ʾāmənām YHWH heḥĕrībū malkē ʾaššūr ʾet-kol-hāʾărāṣōt wəʾet-ʾarṣām

paragraphs.text: וְנָתֹ֥ן אֶת־אֱלֹהֵיהֶ֖ם בָּאֵ֑שׁ כִּי֩ לֹ֨א אֱלֹהִ֜ים הֵ֗מָּה כִּ֣י אִם־מַעֲשֵׂ֧ה יְדֵֽי־אָדָ֛ם עֵ֥ץ וָאֶ֖בֶן וַֽיְאַבְּדֽוּם׃

i18n.en: and have cast their gods into the fire; for they were no gods, but the work of human hands, wood and stone; therefore they have destroyed them.
i18n.he: וְנָתֹ֥ן אֶת־אֱלֹהֵיהֶ֖ם בָּאֵ֑שׁ כִּי֩ לֹ֨א אֱלֹהִ֜ים הֵ֗מָּה כִּ֣י אִם־מַעֲשֵׂ֧ה יְדֵֽי־אָדָ֛ם עֵ֥ץ וָאֶ֖בֶן וַֽיְאַבְּדֽוּם׃

notes.official: *Maʿăśēh yᵉḏê-ʾāḏām* “the work of human hands”: generic *ʾāḏām* is rendered by the adjective “human,” as at 31:3 (overlay `adam-humankind-ish-man-isaiah`). ASV and JPS 1917 have “men's hands,” NJPS “man's handwork” (checked). Isaiah has the infinitive absolute *wᵉnāṯōn* “and have cast,” continuing the finite verb of 37:18, where 2 Kgs 19:18 has the finite *wᵉnāṯᵉnû* (MT, checked); the sense is the same. The burned gods are lower case (overlay `elohim-el-eloah-monotheistic-formula-isaiah`).

paragraphs.translit: wənātōn ʾet-ʾĕlōhēhem bāʾēš kī lōʾ ʾĕlōhīm hēmmāh kī ʾim-maʿăśēh yədē-ʾādām ʿēṣ wāʾeben wayʾabbədūm

paragraphs.text: וְעַתָּה֙ יְהוָ֣ה אֱלֹהֵ֔ינוּ הוֹשִׁיעֵ֖נוּ מִיָד֑וֹ וְיֵֽדְעוּ֙ כָּל־מַמְלְכ֣וֹת הָאָ֔רֶץ כִּֽי־אַתָּ֥ה יְהוָ֖ה לְבַדֶּֽךָ׃

i18n.en: Now therefore, O YHWH our God, save us from his hand, that all the kingdoms of the earth may know that you are YHWH, you alone.”
i18n.he: וְעַתָּה֙ יְהוָ֣ה אֱלֹהֵ֔ינוּ הוֹשִׁיעֵ֖נוּ מִיָד֑וֹ וְיֵֽדְעוּ֙ כָּל־מַמְלְכ֣וֹת הָאָ֔רֶץ כִּֽי־אַתָּ֥ה יְהוָ֖ה לְבַדֶּֽךָ׃

notes.official: *Kî-ʾattāh YHWH lᵉḇaddeḵā* “that you are YHWH, you alone”: 2 Kgs 19:19 reads *kî ʾattāh YHWH ʾĕlōhîm lᵉḇaddeḵā* “that you, YHWH, are God alone,” and adds *nāʾ* after “save us” (MT, checked). NJPS supplies the Kings word, “that You, O LORD, alone [are God],” with the note “Supplied from 2 Kings 19.19” (checked). 1QIsaᵃ is reported to agree with Kings (not verified). ASV and JPS 1917 translate the Isaiah text, and so does the line (overlays `lexical-cruxes-isaiah-37`, `mt-qere-textual-policy-isaiah`).

paragraphs.translit: wəʿattāh YHWH ʾĕlōhēnū hōšīʿēnū miyādō wəyēdəʿū kol-mamləkōt hāʾāreṣ kī-ʾattāh YHWH ləbaddekā

paragraphs.text: וַיִּשְׁלַח֙ יְשַֽׁעְיָ֣הוּ בֶן־אָמ֔וֹץ אֶל־חִזְקִיָּ֖הוּ לֵאמֹ֑ר כֹּֽה־אָמַ֤ר יְהוָה֙ אֱלֹהֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל אֲשֶׁר֙ הִתְפַּלַּ֣לְתָּ אֵלַ֔י אֶל־סַנְחֵרִ֖יב מֶ֥לֶךְ אַשּֽׁוּר׃

i18n.en: Then Isaiah the son of Amoz sent to Hezekiah, saying, “Thus says YHWH, the God of Israel: Because you have prayed to me against Sennacherib king of Assyria,
i18n.he: וַיִּשְׁלַח֙ יְשַֽׁעְיָ֣הוּ בֶן־אָמ֔וֹץ אֶל־חִזְקִיָּ֖הוּ לֵאמֹ֑ר כֹּֽה־אָמַ֤ר יְהוָה֙ אֱלֹהֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל אֲשֶׁר֙ הִתְפַּלַּ֣לְתָּ אֵלַ֔י אֶל־סַנְחֵרִ֖יב מֶ֥לֶךְ אַשּֽׁוּר׃

notes.official: *ʾĂšer hiṯpallaltā ʾēlay ʾel-sanḥērîḇ* “Because you have prayed to me against Sennacherib”: ASV and JPS 1917 (“Whereas thou hast prayed to Me against Sennacherib”) read *ʾăšer* as causal and *ʾel* as hostile. NJPS reads *ʾăšer* as a relative and *ʾel* as “concerning”: “the God of Israel, to whom you have prayed, concerning King Sennacherib” (checked). The line keeps ASV (overlay `lexical-cruxes-isaiah-37`). 2 Kgs 19:20 ends the clause with *šāmaʿtî* “I have heard” (MT, checked), which gives the causal clause its main verb; Isaiah lacks the word, and its sentence runs on into 37:22.

paragraphs.translit: wayyišlaḥ yəšaʿyāhū ben-ʾāmōṣ ʾel-ḥizqiyyāhū lēʾmōr kōh-ʾāmar YHWH ʾĕlōhē yiśrāʾēl ʾăšer hitpallaltā ʾēlay ʾel-sanḥērīb melek ʾaššūr

paragraphs.text: זֶ֣ה הַדָּבָ֔ר אֲשֶׁר־דִּבֶּ֥ר יְהוָ֖ה עָלָ֑יו בָּזָ֨ה לְךָ֜ לָעֲגָ֣ה לְךָ֗ בְּתוּלַת֙ בַּת־צִיּ֔וֹן אַחֲרֶ֙יךָ֙ רֹ֣אשׁ הֵנִ֔יעָה בַּ֖ת יְרוּשָׁלִָֽם׃

i18n.en: this is the word that YHWH has spoken concerning him: The virgin daughter of Zion has despised you and laughed you to scorn; the daughter of Jerusalem has shaken her head at you.
i18n.he: זֶ֣ה הַדָּבָ֔ר אֲשֶׁר־דִּבֶּ֥ר יְהוָ֖ה עָלָ֑יו בָּזָ֨ה לְךָ֜ לָעֲגָ֣ה לְךָ֗ בְּתוּלַת֙ בַּת־צִיּ֔וֹן אַחֲרֶ֙יךָ֙ רֹ֣אשׁ הֵנִ֔יעָה בַּ֖ת יְרוּשָׁלִָֽם׃

notes.official: The taunt over Sennacherib (37:22–29) is verse. *Bāzāh lᵉḵā lāʿăḡāh lᵉḵā* “has despised you and laughed you to scorn”: the perfects are rendered as present perfects with ASV and JPS 1917; NJPS uses the present, “Fair Maiden Zion despises you, She mocks at you” (checked). *ʾAḥărêḵā rōʾš hēnîʿāh* is literally “behind you she has shaken her head,” a gesture made at an enemy as he withdraws; the line keeps ASV's “at you” (overlay `lexical-cruxes-isaiah-37`). *Bᵉṯûlaṯ baṯ-ṣiyyôn* “the virgin daughter of Zion” (ASV, JPS 1917; as 23:12 of Sidon). 2 Kgs 19:21 is identical in MT (checked).

paragraphs.translit: zeh haddābār ʾăšer-dibber YHWH ʿālāyw bāzāh ləkā lāʿăgāh ləkā bətūlat bat-ṣiyyōn ʾaḥărēkā rōʾš hēnīʿāh bat yərūšālim

paragraphs.text: אֶת־מִ֤י חֵרַ֙פְתָּ֙ וְגִדַּ֔פְתָּ וְעַל־מִ֖י הֲרִימ֣וֹתָה קּ֑וֹל וַתִּשָּׂ֥א מָר֛וֹם עֵינֶ֖יךָ אֶל־קְד֥וֹשׁ יִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃

i18n.en: Whom have you defied and blasphemed? And against whom have you raised your voice and lifted up your eyes on high? Against the Holy One of Israel!
i18n.he: אֶת־מִ֤י חֵרַ֙פְתָּ֙ וְגִדַּ֔פְתָּ וְעַל־מִ֖י הֲרִימ֣וֹתָה קּ֑וֹל וַתִּשָּׂ֥א מָר֛וֹם עֵינֶ֖יךָ אֶל־קְד֥וֹשׁ יִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃

notes.official: The line follows ASV and NJPS in reading the verse as one question answered by “Against the Holy One of Israel!” (checked). JPS 1917 ends the question at *qôl* “voice” and makes the rest a statement: “Yea, thou hast lifted up thine eyes on high, Even against the Holy One of Israel!” (checked). The athnach on *qôl* allows that division (overlay `lexical-cruxes-isaiah-37`). *Ḥērap̄tā wᵉgiddap̄tā* “defied and blasphemed” keeps the English of 37:4 and 37:6. 2 Kgs 19:22 has *ʿal-qᵉḏôš* for Isaiah's *ʾel-qᵉḏôš* (MT, checked).

paragraphs.translit: ʾet-mī ḥēraptā wəgiddaptā wəʿal-mī hărīmōtāh qōl wattiśśāʾ mārōm ʿēnēkā ʾel-qədōš yiśrāʾēl

paragraphs.text: בְּיַ֣ד עֲבָדֶיךָ֮ חֵרַ֣פְתָּ ׀ אֲדֹנָי֒ וַתֹּ֗אמֶר בְּרֹ֥ב רִכְבִּ֛י אֲנִ֥י עָלִ֛יתִי מְר֥וֹם הָרִ֖ים יַרְכְּתֵ֣י לְבָנ֑וֹן וְאֶכְרֹ֞ת קוֹמַ֤ת אֲרָזָיו֙ מִבְחַ֣ר בְּרֹשָׁ֔יו וְאָבוֹא֙ מְר֣וֹם קִצּ֔וֹ יַ֖עַר כַּרְמִלּֽוֹ׃

i18n.en: By your servants you have defied the Lord, and you have said, ‘With the multitude of my chariots I have come up to the height of the mountains, to the far reaches of Lebanon; and I will cut down its tall cedars, its choice cypresses; and I will enter its farthest height, the forest of its fruitful field.
i18n.he: בְּיַ֣ד עֲבָדֶיךָ֮ חֵרַ֣פְתָּ ׀ אֲדֹנָי֒ וַתֹּ֗אמֶר בְּרֹ֥ב רִכְבִּ֛י אֲנִ֥י עָלִ֛יתִי מְר֥וֹם הָרִ֖ים יַרְכְּתֵ֣י לְבָנ֑וֹן וְאֶכְרֹ֞ת קוֹמַ֤ת אֲרָזָיו֙ מִבְחַ֣ר בְּרֹשָׁ֔יו וְאָבוֹא֙ מְר֣וֹם קִצּ֔וֹ יַ֖עַר כַּרְמִלּֽוֹ׃

notes.official:
*Yarkᵉṯê lᵉḇānôn* “the far reaches of Lebanon”: ASV and JPS 1917 have “the innermost parts,” NJPS “the remotest parts” (checked). The line uses “the far reaches,” the English that 14:13 and 14:15 give *yarkᵉṯê* (overlay `helel-zaphon-elyon-taunt-isaiah-14`). Both passages are taunts over a king who boasts of going up to the heights (*ʾeʿĕleh*, 14:13; *ʿālîṯî*, 37:24), and the shared English shows that they use the same noun (overlay `lexical-cruxes-isaiah-37`).

*Bᵉrōšāyw* “its choice cypresses” follows 14:8, where the *bᵉrôšîm* rejoice beside the cedars of Lebanon; ASV has “fir-trees,” JPS 1917 “cypress-trees,” NJPS “cypresses” (checked). *Karmillô* “its fruitful field” is the common noun of 10:18, 29:17 and 32:15, not the place name Carmel that 35:2 prints beside Sharon. NJPS has “Its densest forest,” with the note “Lit. ‘Its farmland forest’; exact meaning of Heb. uncertain” (checked). *Mᵉrôm qiṣṣô* “its farthest height” is ASV and JPS 1917.

The tenses follow ASV: “I have come up … and I will cut down … and I will enter.” *Wᵉʾeḵrōṯ* and *wᵉʾāḇôʾ* are imperfects with simple *waw*, which JPS 1917 and NJPS render as past (checked). 2 Kgs 19:23 differs in five places (MT, checked): *bᵉyaḏ malʾāḵêḵā* “by your messengers” for “by your servants”; a ketiv/qere at *bᵉrōḇ*; *mibḥôr* for *mibḥar*; the cohortative *wᵉʾāḇôʾāh* for Isaiah's *wᵉʾāḇôʾ*; and *mᵉlôn qiṣṣōh* “its farthest lodging” for *mᵉrôm qiṣṣô* “its farthest height.”

paragraphs.translit: bəyad ʿăbādēkā ḥēraptā | ʾădōnāy wattōʾmer bərōb rikbī ʾănī ʿālītī mərōm hārīm yarkətē ləbānōn wəʾekrōt qōmat ʾărāzāyw mibḥar bərōšāyw wəʾābōʾ mərōm qiṣṣō yaʿar karmillō

paragraphs.text: אֲנִ֥י קַ֖רְתִּי וְשָׁתִ֣יתִי מָ֑יִם וְאַחְרִב֙ בְּכַף־פְּעָמַ֔י כֹּ֖ל יְאֹרֵ֥י מָצֽוֹר׃

i18n.en: I have dug and drunk water, and with the sole of my feet I will dry up all the rivers of Egypt.’
i18n.he: אֲנִ֥י קַ֖רְתִּי וְשָׁתִ֣יתִי מָ֑יִם וְאַחְרִב֙ בְּכַף־פְּעָמַ֔י כֹּ֖ל יְאֹרֵ֥י מָצֽוֹר׃

notes.official:
*ʾĂnî qartî wᵉšāṯîṯî māyim* “I have dug and drunk water”: 2 Kgs 19:24 adds *zārîm*, “foreign water” (MT, checked), and 1QIsaᵃ is reported to have it too (not verified). The line translates Isaiah's text (overlays `lexical-cruxes-isaiah-37`, `mt-qere-textual-policy-isaiah`). NJPS has “drawn,” with the note “Or ‘dug’; meaning of Heb. uncertain” (checked).

*Kōl yᵉʾōrê māṣôr* “all the rivers of Egypt”: *māṣôr* is a poetic name for Egypt, as at 19:6 (ASV and JPS 1917 “Egypt”; lexica recalled, not verified). The plural *yᵉʾōrîm* is “rivers” where no *nᵉhārôt* stands beside it (central `yeor-nile-egyptian-loanword`, Isaiah clause). At 19:6 the same phrase is “the streams of Egypt” because *nᵉhārôt* is “rivers” in that verse; NJPS has “All the streams of Egypt” here (checked). *Wᵉʾaḥriḇ* “I will dry up” is future with ASV; JPS 1917 and NJPS have the past.

paragraphs.translit: ʾănī qartī wəšātītī māyim wəʾaḥrib bəkap-pəʿāmay kōl yəʾōrē māṣōr

paragraphs.text: הֲלֽוֹא־שָׁמַ֤עְתָּ לְמֵֽרָחוֹק֙ אוֹתָ֣הּ עָשִׂ֔יתִי מִ֥ימֵי קֶ֖דֶם וִיצַרְתִּ֑יהָ עַתָּ֣ה הֲבֵאתִ֔יהָ וּתְהִ֗י לְהַשְׁא֛וֹת גַּלִּ֥ים נִצִּ֖ים עָרִ֥ים בְּצֻרֽוֹת׃

i18n.en: Have you not heard how I have done it long ago, and formed it from ancient times? Now I have brought it to pass, that it should be yours to lay waste fortified cities into ruinous heaps.
i18n.he: הֲלֽוֹא־שָׁמַ֤עְתָּ לְמֵֽרָחוֹק֙ אוֹתָ֣הּ עָשִׂ֔יתִי מִ֥ימֵי קֶ֖דֶם וִיצַרְתִּ֑יהָ עַתָּ֣ה הֲבֵאתִ֔יהָ וּתְהִ֗י לְהַשְׁא֛וֹת גַּלִּ֥ים נִצִּ֖ים עָרִ֥ים בְּצֻרֽוֹת׃

notes.official:
*Wîṣartîhā* “and formed it”: the verb *yṣr* is kept as “form” (central `yatsar`), as at 22:11 *yōṣᵉrāh mērāḥôq* “the one who formed it long ago,” which shares *mērāḥôq* with this verse. JPS 1917 has “fashioned”; NJPS reads the planning sense, “I designed it long ago” (checked). The planning sense is carried by the context (“Have you not heard … long ago”), and the line does not put it into the verb.

*Lᵉhašʾôṯ gallîm niṣṣîm ʿārîm bᵉṣurôṯ* “to lay waste fortified cities into ruinous heaps”: the infinitive clause is difficult, and JPS 1917 and NJPS rearrange it (checked). The line keeps ASV's construal (overlay `lexical-cruxes-isaiah-37`). 2 Kgs 19:25 has *lᵉmîmê* for *mîmê* and the form *lahšôṯ* (MT, checked).

paragraphs.translit: hălōʾ-šāmaʿtā ləmērāḥōq ʾōtāh ʿāśītī mīmē qedem wīṣartīhā ʿattāh hăbēʾtīhā ūtəhī ləhašʾōt gallīm niṣṣīm ʿārīm bəṣurōt

paragraphs.text: וְיֹֽשְׁבֵיהֶן֙ קִצְרֵי־יָ֔ד חַ֖תּוּ וָבֹ֑שׁוּ הָי֞וּ עֵ֤שֶׂב שָׂדֶה֙ וִ֣ירַק דֶּ֔שֶׁא חֲצִ֣יר גַּגּ֔וֹת וּשְׁדֵמָ֖ה לִפְנֵ֥י קָמָֽה׃

i18n.en: Therefore their inhabitants were of small power; they were dismayed and ashamed; they were as the grass of the field, and as the green herb, as the grass on the housetops, and as a field of grain before it is grown up.
i18n.he: וְיֹֽשְׁבֵיהֶן֙ קִצְרֵי־יָ֔ד חַ֖תּוּ וָבֹ֑שׁוּ הָי֞וּ עֵ֤שֶׂב שָׂדֶה֙ וִ֣ירַק דֶּ֔שֶׁא חֲצִ֣יר גַּגּ֔וֹת וּשְׁדֵמָ֖ה לִפְנֵ֥י קָמָֽה׃

notes.official:
*Ḥattû wāḇōšû* “they were dismayed and ashamed”: the same pair as 20:5, “they shall be dismayed and ashamed” (overlay `lexical-cruxes-isaiah-20`). ASV and JPS 1917 have “dismayed and confounded,” NJPS “Dismayed and shamed” (checked). *Qiṣrê-yāḏ* “of small power” (ASV) is literally “short of hand.” 2 Kgs 19:26 has *wayyēḇōšû* for Isaiah's *wāḇōšû* (MT, checked), with no difference of sense.

*Ûšᵉḏēmāh lip̄nê qāmāh* “and as a field of grain before it is grown up”: MT *šᵉḏēmāh* is “field” (cf. 16:8 *šaḏmôṯ ḥešbôn*, MT checked), and ASV supplies “[of grain].” 2 Kgs 19:26 reads *šᵉḏēp̄āh* “blasted” (MT, checked). NJPS follows that reading, “Grass of the roofs that is blasted Before the east wind,” with the note “So ms. 1QIsa; cf. 2 Kings 19.26. The usual reading in our passage means, literally, ‘and a field [?] before standing grain’” (checked). The line translates MT with ASV (overlays `lexical-cruxes-isaiah-37`, `mt-qere-textual-policy-isaiah`).

paragraphs.translit: wəyōšəbēhen qiṣrē-yād ḥattū wābōšū hāyū ʿēśeb śādeh wīraq dešeʾ ḥăṣīr gaggōt ūšədēmāh lipnē qāmāh

paragraphs.text: וְשִׁבְתְּךָ֛ וְצֵאתְךָ֥ וּבוֹאֲךָ֖ יָדָ֑עְתִּי וְאֵ֖ת הִֽתְרַגֶּזְךָ֥ אֵלָֽי׃

i18n.en: But I know your sitting down, and your going out, and your coming in, and your raging against me.
i18n.he: וְשִׁבְתְּךָ֛ וְצֵאתְךָ֥ וּבוֹאֲךָ֖ יָדָ֑עְתִּי וְאֵ֖ת הִֽתְרַגֶּזְךָ֥ אֵלָֽי׃

paragraphs.translit: wəšibtəkā wəṣēʾtəkā ūbōʾăkā yādāʿəttī wəʾēt hitraggezkā ʾēlāy

paragraphs.text: יַ֚עַן הִתְרַגֶּזְךָ֣ אֵלַ֔י וְשַׁאֲנַנְךָ֖ עָלָ֣ה בְאָזְנָ֑י וְשַׂמְתִּ֨י חַחִ֜י בְּאַפֶּ֗ךָ וּמִתְגִּי֙ בִּשְׂפָתֶ֔יךָ וַהֲשִׁ֣יבֹתִ֔יךָ בַּדֶּ֖רֶךְ אֲשֶׁר־בָּ֥אתָ בָּֽהּ׃

i18n.en: Because of your raging against me, and because your arrogance has come up into my ears, I will put my hook in your nose and my bridle in your lips, and I will turn you back by the way by which you came.
i18n.he: יַ֚עַן הִתְרַגֶּזְךָ֣ אֵלַ֔י וְשַׁאֲנַנְךָ֖ עָלָ֣ה בְאָזְנָ֑י וְשַׂמְתִּ֨י חַחִ֜י בְּאַפֶּ֗ךָ וּמִתְגִּי֙ בִּשְׂפָתֶ֔יךָ וַהֲשִׁ֣יבֹתִ֔יךָ בַּדֶּ֖רֶךְ אֲשֶׁר־בָּ֥אתָ בָּֽהּ׃

notes.official:
*Wᵉšaʾănankā ʿālāh ḇᵉʾoznāy* “and because your arrogance has come up into my ears”: *šaʾănān* is “quiet” at 32:18 and 33:20 (overlay `lexical-cruxes-isaiah-33`), where it describes Jerusalem at rest. The same word describes complacent ease at Amos 6:1 (“at ease in Zion”) and stands in parallel with “the proud” at Ps 123:4 (MT and ASV checked). That is its sense here, of the Assyrian king, and ASV has “arrogancy.” The line therefore gives the word two English renderings for its two senses: “quiet” of a dwelling, “arrogance” of a person (overlay `lexical-cruxes-isaiah-37`). JPS 1917 “uproar” and NJPS “tumult” (checked) take the word with the noise of the king's raging; the lexical basis of that reading was not verified.

*Ḥaḥî* “my hook” and *mitgî* “my bridle” (ASV, JPS 1917; NJPS “My bit”) are the gear of a led animal. 2 Kgs 19:28 is identical in sense (MT, checked).

paragraphs.translit: yaʿan hitraggezkā ʾēlay wəšaʾănankā ʿālāh bəʾoznāy wəśamtī ḥaḥī bəʾappekā ūmitgī biśpātēkā wahăšībōtīkā badderek ʾăšer-bāʾtā bāh

paragraphs.text: וְזֶה־לְּךָ֣ הָא֔וֹת אָכ֤וֹל הַשָּׁנָה֙ סָפִ֔יחַ וּבַשָּׁנָ֥ה הַשֵּׁנִ֖ית שָׁחִ֑יס וּבַשָּׁנָ֣ה הַשְּׁלִישִׁ֗ית זִרְע֧וּ וְקִצְר֛וּ וְנִטְע֥וּ כְרָמִ֖ים ואכול [וְאִכְל֥וּ] פִרְיָֽם׃

i18n.en: And this shall be the sign for you: this year you shall eat what grows of itself, and in the second year what springs from that; and in the third year sow and reap, and plant vineyards and eat their fruit.
i18n.he: וְזֶה־לְּךָ֣ הָא֔וֹת אָכ֤וֹל הַשָּׁנָה֙ סָפִ֔יחַ וּבַשָּׁנָ֥ה הַשֵּׁנִ֖ית שָׁחִ֑יס וּבַשָּׁנָ֣ה הַשְּׁלִישִׁ֗ית זִרְע֧וּ וְקִצְר֛וּ וְנִטְע֥וּ כְרָמִ֖ים ואכול [וְאִכְל֥וּ] פִרְיָֽם׃

notes.official:
Ketiv/qere: the ketiv ואכול is the infinitive absolute *ʾāḵôl* “eating,” the qere *wᵉʾiḵlû* the plural imperative “and eat.” The line reads the qere (overlay `mt-qere-textual-policy-isaiah`), as ASV, JPS 1917 and NJPS do (checked). 2 Kgs 19:29 writes *wᵉʾiḵlû* in the text with no ketiv/qere (MT, checked).

*Lᵉḵā* “for you” is singular, addressed to Hezekiah (NJPS note “I.e., Hezekiah,” checked), and the instructions that follow are plural. The infinitive absolute *ʾāḵôl* at the start is rendered as a finite future, “you shall eat,” with ASV. *Sāp̄îaḥ* “what grows of itself” and *šāḥîs* “what springs from that”: Kings spells the second word *sāḥîš* (MT, checked).

paragraphs.translit: wəzeh-ləkā hāʾōt ʾākōl haššānāh sāpīaḥ ūbaššānāh haššēnīt šāḥīs ūbaššānāh haššəlīšīt zirʿū wəqiṣrū wəniṭʿū kərāmīm wʾkwl [wəʾiklū] piryām

paragraphs.text: וְיָ֨סְפָ֜ה פְּלֵיטַ֧ת בֵּית־יְהוּדָ֛ה הַנִּשְׁאָרָ֖ה שֹׁ֣רֶשׁ לְמָ֑טָּה וְעָשָׂ֥ה פְרִ֖י לְמָֽעְלָה׃

i18n.en: And the survivors of the house of Judah who remain shall again take root downward and bear fruit upward.
i18n.he: וְיָ֨סְפָ֜ה פְּלֵיטַ֧ת בֵּית־יְהוּדָ֛ה הַנִּשְׁאָרָ֖ה שֹׁ֣רֶשׁ לְמָ֑טָּה וְעָשָׂ֥ה פְרִ֖י לְמָֽעְלָה׃

notes.official: *Pᵉlêṭaṯ bêṯ-yᵉhûḏāh hannišʾārāh* “the survivors of the house of Judah who remain”: *pᵉlêṭāh* in its collective sense is “survivors,” as at 4:2 and 10:20 (“the survivors of the house of Jacob”; overlay `lexical-cruxes-isaiah-4`). ASV and JPS 1917 have “the remnant that is escaped,” NJPS “the survivors of the House of Judah that have escaped” (checked). Central `pleitah-deliverance-escape-remnant-tradition-cross-corpus` names this verse and 2 Kgs 19:30–31 in its literature, but its wohChoice is the Gen 45:7 “deliverance,” so it is cited here, not extended. 2 Kgs 19:30 is identical (MT, checked).

paragraphs.translit: wəyāsəpāh pəlēṭat bēt-yəhūdāh hannišʾārāh šōreš ləmāṭṭāh wəʿāśāh pərī ləmāʿəlāh

paragraphs.text: כִּ֤י מִירֽוּשָׁלִַ֙ם֙ תֵּצֵ֣א שְׁאֵרִ֔ית וּפְלֵיטָ֖ה מֵהַ֣ר צִיּ֑וֹן קִנְאַ֛ת יְהוָ֥ה צְבָא֖וֹת תַּֽעֲשֶׂה־זֹּֽאת׃ (ס)

i18n.en: For out of Jerusalem shall go forth a remnant, and survivors out of Mount Zion. The zeal of YHWH of hosts will do this.
i18n.he: כִּ֤י מִירֽוּשָׁלִַ֙ם֙ תֵּצֵ֣א שְׁאֵרִ֔ית וּפְלֵיטָ֖ה מֵהַ֣ר צִיּ֑וֹן קִנְאַ֛ת יְהוָ֥ה צְבָא֖וֹת תַּֽעֲשֶׂה־זֹּֽאת׃ (ס)

notes.official: *Šᵉʾērîṯ … ûp̄ᵉlêṭāh* “a remnant … and survivors”: the two remnant nouns of 37:4 and 37:31 stand together in one line (central `she-erit-remnant-cross-corpus-theological-keyword`; *pᵉlêṭāh* as at 37:31). *Qinʾaṯ YHWH ṣᵉḇāʾôṯ taʿăśeh-zōʾṯ* “The zeal of YHWH of hosts will do this” repeats the last sentence of 9:6 word for word, and the line repeats its English; ASV has “will perform this” at both places. In 2 Kgs 19:31 *ṣᵉḇāʾôṯ* is a qere without ketiv, a word read but not written (MT, checked).

paragraphs.translit: kī mīrūšālim tēṣēʾ šəʾērīt ūpəlēṭāh mēhar ṣiyyōn qinʾat YHWH ṣəbāʾōt taʿăśeh-zōʾt (s)

paragraphs.text: לָכֵ֗ן כֹּֽה־אָמַ֤ר יְהוָה֙ אֶל־מֶ֣לֶךְ אַשּׁ֔וּר לֹ֤א יָבוֹא֙ אֶל־הָעִ֣יר הַזֹּ֔את וְלֹֽא־יוֹרֶ֥ה שָׁ֖ם חֵ֑ץ וְלֹֽא־יְקַדְּמֶ֣נָּה מָגֵ֔ן וְלֹֽא־יִשְׁפֹּ֥ךְ עֳלֶ֖יהָ סֹלְלָֽה׃

i18n.en: Therefore thus says YHWH concerning the king of Assyria: He shall not come into this city, nor shoot an arrow there, nor come before it with a shield, nor cast up a mound against it.
i18n.he: לָכֵ֗ן כֹּֽה־אָמַ֤ר יְהוָה֙ אֶל־מֶ֣לֶךְ אַשּׁ֔וּר לֹ֤א יָבוֹא֙ אֶל־הָעִ֣יר הַזֹּ֔את וְלֹֽא־יוֹרֶ֥ה שָׁ֖ם חֵ֑ץ וְלֹֽא־יְקַדְּמֶ֣נָּה מָגֵ֔ן וְלֹֽא־יִשְׁפֹּ֥ךְ עֳלֶ֖יהָ סֹלְלָֽה׃

paragraphs.translit: lākēn kōh-ʾāmar YHWH ʾel-melek ʾaššūr lōʾ yābōʾ ʾel-hāʿīr hazzōʾt wəlōʾ-yōreh šām ḥēṣ wəlōʾ-yəqaddəmennāh māgēn wəlōʾ-yišpōk ʿŏlēhā sōləlāh

paragraphs.text: בַּדֶּ֥רֶךְ אֲשֶׁר־בָּ֖א בָּ֣הּ יָשׁ֑וּב וְאֶל־הָעִ֥יר הַזֹּ֛את לֹ֥א יָב֖וֹא נְאֻם־יְהוָֽה׃

i18n.en: By the way that he came, by the same he shall return, and he shall not come into this city, says YHWH.
i18n.he: בַּדֶּ֥רֶךְ אֲשֶׁר־בָּ֖א בָּ֣הּ יָשׁ֑וּב וְאֶל־הָעִ֥יר הַזֹּ֛את לֹ֥א יָב֖וֹא נְאֻם־יְהוָֽה׃

notes.official: 2 Kgs 19:33 has the imperfect *yāḇōʾ* “by the way that he comes” where Isaiah has the perfect *bāʾ* “came” (MT, checked).

paragraphs.translit: badderek ʾăšer-bāʾ bāh yāšūb wəʾel-hāʿīr hazzōʾt lōʾ yābōʾ nəʾum-YHWH

paragraphs.text: וְגַנּוֹתִ֛י עַל־הָעִ֥יר הַזֹּ֖את לְהֽוֹשִׁיעָ֑הּ לְמַֽעֲנִ֔י וּלְמַ֖עַן דָּוִ֥ד עַבְדִּֽי׃ (ס)

i18n.en: For I will protect this city to save it, for my own sake and for the sake of David my servant.”
i18n.he: וְגַנּוֹתִ֛י עַל־הָעִ֥יר הַזֹּ֖את לְהֽוֹשִׁיעָ֑הּ לְמַֽעֲנִ֔י וּלְמַ֖עַן דָּוִ֥ד עַבְדִּֽי׃ (ס)

notes.official: *Wᵉḡannôṯî ʿal-hāʿîr hazzōʾṯ* “For I will protect this city”: *gnn* is “protect,” as at 31:5 (overlay `lexical-cruxes-isaiah-31`). ASV and JPS 1917 have “defend,” NJPS “protect” (checked). 2 Kgs 19:34 has *ʾel-hāʿîr* for *ʿal-hāʿîr* (MT, checked).

paragraphs.translit: wəgannōtī ʿal-hāʿīr hazzōʾt ləhōšīʿāh ləmaʿănī ūləmaʿan dāwid ʿabdī (s)

paragraphs.text: וַיֵּצֵ֣א ׀ מַלְאַ֣ךְ יְהוָ֗ה וַיַּכֶּה֙ בְּמַחֲנֵ֣ה אַשּׁ֔וּר מֵאָ֛ה וּשְׁמֹנִ֥ים וַחֲמִשָּׁ֖ה אָ֑לֶף וַיַּשְׁכִּ֣ימוּ בַבֹּ֔קֶר וְהִנֵּ֥ה כֻלָּ֖ם פְּגָרִ֥ים מֵתִֽים׃

i18n.en: And the messenger of YHWH went out and struck down in the camp of Assyria a hundred and eighty-five thousand; and when people arose early in the morning, behold, all of them were dead bodies.
i18n.he: וַיֵּצֵ֣א ׀ מַלְאַ֣ךְ יְהוָ֗ה וַיַּכֶּה֙ בְּמַחֲנֵ֣ה אַשּׁ֔וּר מֵאָ֛ה וּשְׁמֹנִ֥ים וַחֲמִשָּׁ֖ה אָ֑לֶף וַיַּשְׁכִּ֣ימוּ בַבֹּ֔קֶר וְהִנֵּ֥ה כֻלָּ֖ם פְּגָרִ֥ים מֵתִֽים׃

notes.official:
*Malʾaḵ YHWH* “the messenger of YHWH” (central `malakh-yhwh-messenger`, which already lists this verse and the parallel 2 Kgs 19:35). ASV and JPS 1917 have “the angel of Jehovah / of the LORD,” NJPS “an angel of the LORD” (checked). Isaiah renders *malʾāḵ* “messenger” at every other site (14:32; 18:2; 33:7; 37:9, 14), and the central entry keeps the noun's literal sense without deciding what kind of being is meant. The line follows the entry; overlay `lexical-cruxes-isaiah-37` records the decision, which overlay `lexical-cruxes-isaiah-33` had left open.

*Wayyaškîmû ḇabbōqer* “when people arose early in the morning”: the verb has no expressed subject, and the subject is not the Assyrians who died. ASV and JPS 1917 supply “men”; NJPS recasts the clause, “the following morning” (checked). The line supplies the neutral “people” (house rule for generic human nouns; overlay `adam-humankind-ish-man-isaiah`), so that the clause cannot be read of the dead. *Pᵉḡārîm mēṯîm* is “dead bodies” (ASV; JPS 1917 and NJPS “dead corpses”). 2 Kgs 19:35 has the short form *wayyaḵ* for Isaiah's *wayyakkeh* and no *waw* before *šᵉmōnîm* (MT, checked), without difference of sense. It also opens with *wayᵉhî ballaylāh hahûʾ* “And it came to pass that night”, which NJPS supplies in brackets, “[That night],” with the note “Supplied from 2 Kings 19.35” (checked).

**Wheel of Heaven reading (speculative).** The canon does not cite Isa 37:36 or 2 Kgs 19:35 (data-library *The Book Which Tells the Truth*, checked). It does read the *malʾaḵ YHWH* of another passage as one of the Elohim: TBWTT 3:72–73 introduces Judg 6:21, “the angel of Yahweh put forth the end of the staff,” with the sentence “one of the creators is again in contact with a man named Gideon.” TBWTT 3:75 then explains the rout of an enemy camp in Judg 7 as the effect of amplified sound. A Wheel of Heaven reading carries those two readings over to this verse and takes the messenger who strikes the Assyrian camp as an envoy of the Elohim acting by technical means. The transfer is the project's, not the canon's, and the translated line does not depend on it.

notes.official: The names follow ASV (wave ruling 3): Nisroch, Adrammelech, Sharezer, Ararat, Esar-haddon. ASV hyphenates “Esar-haddon”; JPS 1917 and NJPS have “Sarezer” and “Esarhaddon” (checked). *ʾEreṣ ʾărārāṭ* “the land of Ararat” is the region known from Assyrian sources as Urartu (recalled, not verified); central `harei-ararat`, which governs “the mountains of Ararat,” is not applied. *Nisrōḵ ʾĕlōhāyw* “Nisroch his god” is lower case (overlay `elohim-el-eloah-monotheistic-formula-isaiah`); the deity is not otherwise attested by that name, and proposed identifications were not verified. *Bêṯ* is “the house” (ASV, JPS 1917; NJPS “temple”) (overlay `lexical-cruxes-isaiah-37`). 2 Kgs 19:37 has *bānāyw* “his sons” only as a qere without ketiv, where Isaiah writes the word (MT, checked).
